text.p: Boeing Commercial Airplane Group said Thursday it has accelerated a planned Boeing 737 production increase in response to increased market demand.

The Boeing Co unit said the twinjet will be produced at a rate of 17 airplanes per month by the third quarter of 1997, six months ahead of the previous schedule announced in June. The 737, which is currently produced at a rate of 8.5 airplanes per month, will build up to this new level by increasing to 1O airplanes per month by January 1997, then to 12 airplanes per month by the second quarter of 1997.
Boeing said it also is developing plans and working with suppliers to ensure that it can respond to an even greater, future demand for the 737.
